text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Eurotunnel reaches outline agreement on debt restructuring with six leading bank lenders in the form of a debt-for-equity swap. Other banks and shareholders must in turn ratify agreement.(Les Echos, la Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- Paris Motor Show to open to the public tomorrow, French carmakers to apply competitive pricing policy to support sales after the expiry of a government incentive scheme for buyers of new cars, which boosted September sales by 85.7 percent. (Les Echos, la Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- European countries compete over planned budget austerity for the sake of single currency, President Jacques Chirac raises doubts about Italy's ability to be part of the first group of countries implementing the move to a single currency.
-- Labour Minister Jacques Barrot calls for an improved professional training system, will present bill in early 1997.

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis submits to National Assembly a five-year austerity and spending cuts plan designed to curb budget deficit to 190 billion francs in 2001 from an expected 284 billion in 1997.

-- Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) posts a 533-million-franc profit for the first half, returns to profitability ahead of a privatisation in which 67 percent of its capital is to be sold. Bidders' indentities have yet to be revealed.
-- CFDT trade union chief Nicole Notat wins leadership of unemeployment benefit fund Unedic.
-- Retail group Leclerc launches information campaign to present future euro currency to consumers in daily life situations, backed by European Commission.

-- Thomson-CSF privatisation through private placement to be effective in two weeks, Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Groupe MMBP.PA to bid for the 70-billion-franc-turnover electronics and defence group.

-- Government-approved merger project betweeen Alcatel Alsthom subsidiary GEC-Alsthom and nuclear-plant manufacturer Framatome may help Alcatel finance bid for Thomson-CSF, through Framatome cash reserve.
-- President Jacques Chirac's remarks expressing doubt about Italy's ability to meet European single currency timetable withdrawn after Italian complaints.
